questions.questionText: Find the greatest number that divides 200 and 317 leaving a remainder of 5 in each case.
questions.explanation: Subtract the remainder: 200−5 = 195, 317−5 = 312. Required number = HCF = 39.

questions.questionText: What is the greatest number that divides 173 and 132 leaving remainders 2 and 6 respectively?
Find the greatest number that divides 243, 339 and 411 leaving a remainder of 3 in each case.
questions.explanation: Subtract the remainder: 243−3 = 240, 339−3 = 336, 411−3 = 408. Required number = HCF = 24.

questions.questionText: Find the greatest number that divides 271 and 505 leaving a remainder of 1 in each case.
questions.explanation: Subtract the remainder: 271−1 = 270, 505−1 = 504. Required number = HCF = 18.

questions.questionText: Find the greatest number that divides 101, 129 and 192 leaving a remainder of 3 in each case.
questions.explanation: Subtract the remainder: 101−3 = 98, 129−3 = 126, 192−3 = 189. Required number = HCF = 7.

questions.questionText: What is the greatest number that divides 57 and 79 leaving remainders 1 and 2 respectively?
What is the greatest number that divides 421 and 339 leaving remainders 1 and 3 respectively?
Find the greatest number that divides 633, 737 and 614 leaving remainders 3, 2 and 5 respectively.
Find the greatest number which divides 147, 394 and 446 and leaves the same remainder in each case.
questions.explanation: Same remainder → the number divides every difference. 394−147 = 247, 446−147 = 299. HCF = 13.

questions.questionText: What is the sum of the digits of the greatest number that divides 50 and 458 leaving remainder 2 in each case?
questions.shortcut: Find the HCF of the reduced numbers, then add digits.

questions.questionText: Find the greatest number which divides 261, 295 and 584 and leaves the same remainder in each case.
questions.explanation: Same remainder → the number divides every difference. 295−261 = 34, 584−261 = 323. HCF = 17.

Find the greatest number that divides 257, 264 and 256 leaving remainders 5, 3 and 4 respectively.
Find the greatest number which divides 318, 354 and 450 and leaves the same remainder in each case.
questions.explanation: Same remainder → the number divides every difference. 354−318 = 36, 450−318 = 132. HCF = 12.

questions.questionText: What is the sum of the digits of the greatest number that divides 676 and 781 leaving remainder 4 in each case?
questions.shortcut: Find the HCF of the reduced numbers, then add digits.

questions.questionText: Find the greatest number which divides 402, 652 and 852 and leaves the same remainder in each case.
questions.explanation: Same remainder → the number divides every difference. 652−402 = 250, 852−402 = 450. HCF = 50.

questions.questionText: Find the greatest number that divides 32, 105 and 44 leaving remainders 2, 3 and 2 respectively.
Find the greatest number which divides 78, 803 and 828 and leaves the same remainder in each case.
questions.explanation: Same remainder → the number divides every difference. 803−78 = 725, 828−78 = 750. HCF = 25.

questions.questionText: A number N divides 514, 577 and 110 leaving remainders 4, 7 and 5 respectively. If N is as large as possible, what is the remainder when 1201 is divided by N?
questions.explanation: Largest N = HCF(510, 570, 105) = 15. Each number leaves its own remainder, so the sum leaves (16) mod 15 = 1.
questions.shortcut: Remainder of the sum = sum of remainders (mod N).

questions.questionText: How many different numbers divide 424 and 241 leaving remainders 4 and 1 respectively?
questions.explanation: Any such number divides HCF(420, 240) = 60 and must exceed the larger remainder 4. Divisors of 60 greater than 4: 8.
questions.shortcut: Divisors of the HCF that exceed every remainder.

questions.questionText: How many different numbers divide 830 and 290 leaving remainders 2 and 2 respectively?
questions.explanation: Any such number divides HCF(828, 288) = 36 and must exceed the larger remainder 2. Divisors of 36 greater than 2: 7.
questions.shortcut: Divisors of the HCF that exceed every remainder.

questions.questionText: How many different numbers divide 651 and 410 leaving remainders 3 and 2 respectively?
questions.explanation: Any such number divides HCF(648, 408) = 24 and must exceed the larger remainder 3. Divisors of 24 greater than 3: 5.
questions.shortcut: Divisors of the HCF that exceed every remainder.
